title_en: Inha University's 'DOK4' wins grand prize at AAM Tech Challenge
summary_en: [ZD Net Korea] The Aerospace Administration, along with Jinju City, held the 24th Korea Robotic Aircraft Contest (AAM (Future Air Mobility) Tech Challenge) at the Jinju Air Force Training Command in Gyeongsangnam-do on the 5th. It was prepared to improve the innovative design sense of personnel related to domestic future air transportation (drones, AAM, etc.) and to verify the ability to develop advanced autonomous flight algorithms. The event was organized by the Korea Aerospace Industry Association and the Korea Aerospace University Air Drone. The Innovation Convergence Business Team was in charge. A total of 80 teams participated in the competition, including the preliminary round. The overall system development status, autonomous flight implementation technology, mission performance feasibility, safety devices, etc. were comprehensively verified and evaluated by dividing them into regular and intermediate categories. 12 university (graduate school) teams from across the country advanced to the finals. In the regular category, they will perform the ‘vertical takeoff and landing fixed-wing AAM rescue mission.’ Mainly focused on graduate students. This competition is characterized by the introduction of a distress rescue mission scenario in preparation for the commercialization of AAM. The regular category grand prize (Aerospace Administration Commissioner's Award) was won by Inha University's DOK 4 team, and the grand prize (Jinju Mayor's Award) was won by Hanseo University's HACUS team.
